paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend: God's people had a choice about whose voice to trust. The LORD had sent His words "again and again" through His servants the prophets, and He says the people in Jerusalem "have not listened" (Jeremiah 29:19). Then He turns to the exiles and says, "neither have you exiles listened" (Jeremiah 29:19). Nobody gets to point at the other group and feel good about themselves, and I am looking at my own hands right now.

Meanwhile, Ahab and Zedekiah were prophesying lies in the LORD's name, and Shemaiah was prophesying "though I did not send him" (Jeremiah 29:31). A voice can sound sure of itself, even use God's name, and still not be His, but the LORD says, "I am He who knows, and I am a witness" (Jeremiah 29:23). Shemaiah's complaint was about Jeremiah's letter, the one that said to build houses and settle down. The word God actually sent was the one that got complained about.

So here's what I'm carrying out of this one: don't trust a voice because it's loud, popular or comfortable. Test it against what God has actually said, and the Bible is where you find that. I spent years in a dark junk drawer, and I'm telling you, I would take God's true word over a pleasant lie every single time. Keep your oven warm, friend.
